request.system: You are a senior clinical coder in an Australian public hospital with fifteen years of experience coding inpatient episodes in ICD-10-AM. You are careful, conservative, and you never invent a code you are not sure of the chapter for.

messages.content:
Code the episode of care below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed. Give the three-character ICD-10-AM category for the principal diagnosis.

Hospital course:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY:

Admission Date: [DATE]
Discharge Date: [DATE]

Patient Name: [NAME]
Patient ID: [ID]

Hospital Course Summary:

The patient, a 38-year-old Asian male, was admitted with dyspnea and a productive cough that was diagnosed as pneumonia with subsequent atelectasis of the right middle and lower lobes. Upon transfer to our facility, a CT scan revealed an endobronchial mass obstructing the right bronchus intermedius. After initial treatment with broad-spectrum antibiotics, a rigid bronchoscopy procedure was performed to remove the endobronchial tumor and prevent recurrence through ablation with a diode laser. Pathologically, the removed tumor was identified as bronchial myelolipoma with no evidence of hematologic disorder or endocrine abnormalities. Follow-up bronchoscopies after 3 and 12 months showed no recurrence of the tumor, and the patient's accompanying symptoms such as cough, sputum, and dyspnea improved immediately following the procedure.
Final Diagnoses: [diagnosis section withheld]
Treatment:

1. Broad-spectrum antibiotics for obstructive pneumonia.
2. Rigid bronchoscopy under general anesthesia to remove the endobronchial tumor.
3. Ablation with a diode laser to prevent recurrence.

Condition at Discharge:

The patient has shown a significant improvement in his condition since the bronchoscopy procedure and has no active symptoms related to the previously diagnosed conditions. No further treatment is required, and the patient can be discharged at this time.

Discharge Medications:

No medications are required at the time of discharge.

Follow-up Plan:

Follow-up appointments with a primary care physician are recommended to ensure adequate follow-up of the patient's condition and to monitor for any potential recurrence of bronchial myelolipoma in the future.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
This is a rare benign endobronchial tumour, bronchial myelolipoma, causing obstructive pneumonia and atelectasis. The tumour was established after investigation as the condition chiefly responsible for the admission. The pneumonia and atelectasis are consequences of it, and the symptoms resolved after the tumour was removed.

Myelolipoma is a benign neoplasm of fat and haematopoietic tissue, morphology code M8870/0. For a benign neoplasm of the bronchus, ICD-10-AM places the site in Chapter II at D14.3 (Benign neoplasm of bronchus and lung), within category D14 (Benign neoplasm of middle ear and respiratory system).

The alternative would be D36 (benign neoplasm of other and unspecified sites), but D14 is the more specific category because the site is the bronchus. The pneumonia (J18 or J69) and atelectasis (J98.1) would be secondary diagnoses.

CODE: D14
